$comment: NEW-58 (exponentialTalk (g)): THE screen ring buffer (`screen memory`) of the voice device and its host tool `get_screenshots`. Desktop only, so ONE implementation replays this (apps/desktop/crates/screen, `cargo test -p screen`); voice.json (`trayMenu`, `railVoice`) and voice-policy.json (`tools`) carry its two client-facing bits. SWITCH: device-local, never synced, kept across restarts like the tray's Mute (#NEW-86): the tray's check item `copy.tray` (after Wake word, before Mute; voice.json `trayMenu` with context `screenMemory` {on, paused}) and the rail voice menu's same row; default off; only on the member's voice device (no tray, no capture elsewhere); turning it off deletes the buffer (frames + index rows); another voice device or account turns it off and deletes the buffer; a sign-out or an account change deletes it whether the switch is on or not; at start-up with the switch off a buffer left on disk is deleted; the stops and deletes run off the UI thread, in order; a stop or delete cancels a start still waiting (the Linux portal's dialog) instead of waiting behind it, and the capturer that start opens later is closed at once. While on and capturing the item reads `copy.tray`; while paused it reads `copy.tray` + ` · ` + `copy.paused`. CAPTURE (in the IDE process, never a helper): every WORK display (work-screen.json: the picked display, or Auto = every display without a fullscreen app; a picked display that is gone or no work display = no capture that tick) once every `capture.intervalMs` plus the focused window's display (when a work display) at once whenever the focused window or its title changes (`capture.focusPollMs` poll, ONE window-list read: the focused window's app id + app name + title + rect, the work displays, each display's top window, every on-screen window per display it overlaps with its rect); a display whose top window matches `denylist` is skipped. MASK: every other window on a captured display matching `denylist` is filled black over its whole rect there (also where another window covers it) before the hash and in the stored picture; a frame where one cannot be placed (the reading's display size is not the frame's) is dropped. LABEL: the frame of the display holding the focused window carries its app name and title; another display's frame its top window's app and title, else empty (the dedupe compares these). LABEL, MASK, crop and the pause check read the window-list reading NEAREST the frame's `at` (readings kept 3 s; MASK also adds the newest), so a frame the OS captured before a focus change carries the earlier label; none then = dropped. STAMP: a frame's `at` = when the OS captured or delivered it (macOS the sample's presentation time, Windows the frame's time, PipeWire the delivery), else the grab. STALE: after ANY resume (the pause ends, a display comes back into capture) only frames DELIVERED at or after the resume + `capture.intervalMs` are taken, so a buffer the OS still holds from before (a vault) is never stored with the new label; FRESH: once resume + intervalMs has passed, a display that delivered nothing since is captured once, live (macOS 14+ an SCScreenshotManager sample through the stream's filter, Windows the GDI read, X11 the root read; older macOS and Wayland: its next change), so a still screen is stored once after a resume; macOS ScreenCaptureKit (SCStream per display, minimumFrameInterval = intervalMs, the IDE's own windows excluded), Linux the xdg ScreenCast portal + PipeWire (one session for every monitor, `persist_mode` 2 with the restore token kept in the IDE's settings dir so the portal asks once; X11 without a portal reads the root window like the computer crate: the work displays only, each at most once per intervalMs, 32-bit BGRX lent unconverted), Windows Graphics Capture (one session per monitor, the yellow border off where the OS allows; a delivery is copied once and lent to the hash, never cloned per grab; without the OS's minimum update interval at most one copy per intervalMs, a skipped change read live by the next grab). HASH (`hashCases`, images generated from `pattern`: `solid` = `rgb` everywhere; `split` = black for x < width/2 (integer division), else white; `checker` = black where (x / cell + y / cell) is even, else white; `gradientX` = grey v = 255 * x / (width - 1) (integer); `gradientY` = (v, 0, 255 - v) with v = 255 * y / (height - 1)): luma Y = (299 R + 587 G + 114 B) / 1000 (integer); box-downscale to 64 x 64 (target pixel (i, j) = the integer mean over source x = x0, x0 + kx, … < x1 with [x0, x1) = [i*W/64, max((i+1)*W/64, i*W/64 + 1)), kx = max(1, W / 256), and y likewise with ky = max(1, H / 256), integer division: ~4 x 4 samples a box; a MASKed pixel reads 0); the 64 x 64 splits into 8 x 8 blocks of 8 x 8; bit k (row-major, the first block is the most significant bit) = 64 * blockSum_k > totalSum; the hash = the 64 bits as 16 lowercase hex digits. DEDUPE (`dedupeCases`): a frame is DROPPED when the last KEPT frame of the same display has the same app id and window title and a Hamming distance <= `dedupe.maxDistance`; every other frame is kept. STORE = what TOOL returns: a kept frame is cut to its focused-window rect when it has one on that display at least `tool.minCrop` pixels each way (a tab-hover strip or a tooltip that holds the focus keeps the whole frame), scaled so its long edge is at most `tool.maxEdge` (never up; `fitCases`), and stored as a lossy WebP (`store.webpQuality`, libwebp method 0) under `<data dir>/screen/<UTC yyyyMMdd-HH>/<at ms>-<display>.webp` (one directory per hour) plus one row in the desktop's SQLite `screen_frames` (at ms, display number (1-based, the computer crate's order), app id, window title, hash, path, the frame's width and height, the focused window's rect within the frame when it lies on that display, else null). ENCODE: the capture thread only hashes; one batch per grab of the kept frames goes to ONE encode worker below normal priority (macOS QoS utility, Linux nice 10, Windows below normal) that cuts, scales, encodes and stores, then rests t x (100 - `store.encodePercent`) / encodePercent after a batch that took t of its CPU. SKIP IF BUSY: while the worker works or rests, a grab's frames are dropped and the dedupe does NOT advance, so the next tick retries the change (grabbing those displays' latest frame again). RETENTION (`retentionCases`): once every `capture.intervalMs`, paused or not, rows with at < now - `retentionMs` are deleted with their files, and an hour directory left empty is removed; at start-up the same sweep runs first, and files without a row are deleted; TOOL never returns a frame older than that (`from` is clamped to now - retentionMs). PAUSE (`pauseCases`): capture stops (no frame, not even the 1 s one) while the focused window matches `denylist` (app id (the macOS bundle id where known, else the app name) or app name contains one of `denylist.apps`, or the title contains one of `denylist.titles`; both case-insensitive), while there is no focused-window reading (no window list, focus off every display; fail closed: on Wayland the computer crate has no window list, so screen memory never captures there and its tray and rail row is hidden (voice.json `screenMemory` absent)) or while the pause hotkey holds it (#NEW-57); it resumes with the next tick after the focus leaves it (STALE); `paused` is what the tray item shows. TOOL: the IDE serves a loopback MCP server `screen` (the computer crate's pattern: one endpoint, a per-run bearer token) with ONE tool `get_screenshots`, attached only to the member's conversation session with the voice agent (`voicePolicy` root) on the voice device while screen memory is on; voice-policy.json tiers `mcp__screen__get_screenshots` `auto` (local and read-only). Arguments (`tool.inputSchema`): `from` and `to` (RFC 3339; `to` defaults to now, `from` to `to` - `tool.defaultSpanSeconds`), optional `filter` (case-insensitive substring of the app id or the title). SELECT (`selectCases`): the kept frames with from <= at <= to of a display that is a work display NOW, matching the filter, by time; more than `tool.maxFrames` = indexes round(i * (n - 1) / (maxFrames - 1)) for i in 0..maxFrames (round half away from zero). Each frame's stored WebP is returned as it is (`image/webp`, never re-encoded to PNG) after a text line `{at} · {app} — {title}` (at = RFC 3339 UTC, seconds); SIZE (counted as base64 characters): a frame over `tool.maxImageBytes` is re-encoded at a lower quality, then smaller, until it fits; while the images together exceed `tool.maxTotalBytes` the middle frame is dropped, and a last text `copy.trimmed` says how many; none = the text `copy.none` with {from} {to}; screen memory off = `copy.off`. The description stays within `tool.descriptionMaxChars` (the per-tool MCP budget). Targets: < 2 % of a core at 1 fps on two displays, also while the screen changes every second (measured, M4 Pro: two 3456 x 2234 displays of dense text changing every second 0.6 %, two 5120 x 2880 0.9 %, 11-13 % without the rest; a Safari page paged every 0.5 s on one 3456 x 2234 display 1.2 %; a still screen 0.2 %; the subsampled hash 0.11 ms a frame at 3456 x 2234 and 5120 x 2880, 3.1 and 3.6 ms reading every pixel). TRADE-OFF (owner decision 2026-10-28, the 2 % budget wins): a screen that changes all the time (video, scrolling) keeps a frame every few seconds instead of every second, while focus and title changes are still grabbed at once.
